questions.prompt: Which set best shows the main components of Integrated Science?
questions.correctAnswer: Biology, chemistry, and physics
questions.explanation: Integrated Science brings together ideas from biology, chemistry, and physics to explain natural events and solve problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the components of Integrated Science as a field of study.

questions.prompt: A learner explains why a sufuria handle gets hot when cooking. Which component of Integrated Science is mainly involved?
questions.correctAnswer: Physics
questions.explanation: Physics studies energy, heat, forces, motion, electricity, magnetism, and related changes.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate Integrated Science knowledge to everyday situations.

questions.prompt: Which career is most directly linked to knowledge of living things and body systems?
questions.correctAnswer: Nurse
questions.explanation: Nursing uses biological knowledge about the human body, health, disease prevention, and care.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate knowledge and skills in Integrated Science to career opportunities.

questions.prompt: Integrated Science can help learners make safer decisions about electricity, chemicals, health, and the environment.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Science knowledge supports safe, evidence-based choices in daily life.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the importance of Integrated Science in daily life.

questions.prompt: Which activity best shows the chemistry part of Integrated Science?
options: Testing whether lemon juice is acidic
Drawing a map of a village
questions.correctAnswer: Testing whether lemon juice is acidic
questions.explanation: Chemistry studies substances, their properties, and how they change, including acids and bases.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of biology, chemistry, and physics in daily activities.

questions.prompt: A class studies the skin, kidneys, and menstruation. Which component of Integrated Science are they mainly learning?
questions.correctAnswer: Biology
questions.explanation: Biology studies living things and life processes, including human body systems.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the biology component of Integrated Science.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner connect science lessons to problems in the community?
options: Science skills can guide practical solutions
Science facts are only for examinations
questions.correctAnswer: Science skills can guide practical solutions
questions.explanation: Scientific inquiry helps learners observe problems, collect evidence, and choose workable solutions.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Integrated Science knowledge to solve everyday problems.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to know whether a local stream is safe for household use. Which first action is most scientific?
options: Observe and test water samples using safe procedures
Assume clear water is always safe
Ask only one friend for an opinion
questions.correctAnswer: Observe and test water samples using safe procedures
questions.explanation: A scientific approach starts with careful observation, safe testing, and evidence before making a conclusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Use scientific inquiry to investigate real-life situations.

questions.prompt: Which item is the best example of personal protective equipment in a school laboratory?
questions.correctAnswer: Safety goggles
questions.explanation: Safety goggles protect the eyes from splashes, dust, and small flying particles during practical work.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify protective equipment used in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: A learner should taste an unknown chemical to identify it during a science practical.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Unknown chemicals may be poisonous or corrosive, so tasting chemicals is unsafe.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety precautions when handling laboratory chemicals.

questions.prompt: What should learners do first when a chemical spills on a laboratory bench?
options: Smell it closely to identify it
questions.correctAnswer: Inform the teacher immediately
questions.explanation: The teacher can guide safe cleanup using the correct materials and protective equipment.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate safety measures for common laboratory accidents.

questions.prompt: Which laboratory rule helps prevent burns when heating a liquid in a test tube?
options: Point the mouth of the test tube away from people
Fill the test tube completely to the top
Hold the hot tube with bare fingers
Look directly into the heated liquid
questions.correctAnswer: Point the mouth of the test tube away from people
questions.explanation: Heated liquid can splash or boil suddenly, so the opening should face away from learners.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety precautions when heating substances in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: Which hazard is most likely caused by a wet floor in the laboratory?
questions.correctAnswer: Slipping and falling
questions.explanation: Water or other liquids on the floor reduce friction and increase the chance of slipping.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common hazards in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: A learner's sleeve catches a small flame during a practical. Which response is safest?
options: Stop, drop, and roll while alerting the teacher
Pour unknown chemicals on the sleeve
Hide the accident to avoid trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Stop, drop, and roll while alerting the teacher
questions.explanation: Stopping, dropping, and rolling helps smother flames, while alerting the teacher brings quick help.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate first aid measures for common laboratory accidents.

questions.prompt: Why should chemical containers be clearly labelled?
options: To prevent wrong use and accidents
To allow learners to mix them freely
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent wrong use and accidents
questions.explanation: Clear labels help users identify substances, hazards, and correct handling instructions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of safe storage and labelling of chemicals.

questions.prompt: Broken glass should be picked up using bare hands so that it is removed quickly.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Broken glass can cut the skin and should be handled with a brush, dustpan, or other safe tool.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety measures when handling broken apparatus.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows responsibility after finishing a laboratory practical?
options: Clean the work area and return apparatus safely
Leave used apparatus on the bench
Throw all materials into the sink
questions.correctAnswer: Clean the work area and return apparatus safely
questions.explanation: Cleaning and returning apparatus keeps the laboratory safe and ready for the next users.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate responsible behaviour in the laboratory.

questions.prompt: During group work, one learner wants to test an unapproved reaction. What should the group do?
options: Try it quickly before the teacher sees
Mix extra chemicals to compare results
Let the learner work alone in a corner
questions.correctAnswer: Follow only the teacher-approved procedure
questions.explanation: Unapproved reactions can cause harm, so practical work should follow safe instructions.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate safe and unsafe behaviour during laboratory investigations.

questions.prompt: Which science skill is used when a learner notes that a liquid is blue and has a sharp smell without tasting it?
questions.correctAnswer: Observation
questions.explanation: Observation uses senses and tools to gather information safely about an object or event.
questions.learningOutcome: Use observation as a basic science skill.

questions.prompt: A learner says, 'If the water is heated for longer, it will become hotter.' What science skill is being shown?
questions.correctAnswer: Prediction
questions.explanation: A prediction states what is expected to happen based on prior knowledge or evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Make predictions during scientific investigations.

questions.prompt: Which tool should be used to measure the temperature of warm water?
questions.correctAnswer: Thermometer
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius or another temperature scale.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable tools for measuring physical quantities.

questions.prompt: Why should results from an experiment be recorded in a table?
options: A table makes results easier to compare
A table changes wrong results into right ones
A table removes the need for observation
A table keeps apparatus hot for longer
questions.correctAnswer: A table makes results easier to compare
questions.explanation: Tables organize data in rows and columns so patterns and differences can be seen more clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Communicate science information using tables.

questions.prompt: In a fair test on plant growth, which variable should be changed if the learner is testing the effect of light?
options: Type of soil, water, and pot all at once
questions.correctAnswer: Amount of light
questions.explanation: A fair test changes one factor at a time while keeping other important conditions similar.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan a fair test by identifying variables.

questions.prompt: A learner measures the mass of salt as 20 g before dissolving it. Which quantity was measured?
questions.correctAnswer: Mass
questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in a substance and is commonly measured in grams or kilograms.
questions.learningOutcome: Measure and record mass using appropriate units.

questions.prompt: Repeating an investigation can help check whether the results are reliable.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Repeated trials can reveal mistakes and show whether results are consistent.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of repeated trials in scientific investigations.

questions.prompt: A class records these temperatures: 22 degrees C, 24 degrees C, 26 degrees C, and 28 degrees C. What trend is shown?
questions.correctAnswer: The temperature is increasing
questions.explanation: Each value is greater than the previous one, so the recorded temperature rises over time.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret simple data from a scientific investigation.

questions.prompt: Which statement is a conclusion rather than an observation?
options: The salt dissolved faster in hot water than in cold water
The water in beaker A is clear
questions.correctAnswer: The salt dissolved faster in hot water than in cold water
questions.explanation: A conclusion explains what the results mean after comparing observations or measurements.
questions.learningOutcome: Draw simple conclusions from investigation results.

questions.prompt: A learner designs an investigation to compare two water filters. Which evidence would best support the conclusion?
options: Clear records of water appearance before and after filtering
questions.correctAnswer: Clear records of water appearance before and after filtering
questions.explanation: Useful evidence must relate directly to what the investigation is testing.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate evidence used to support a scientific conclusion.

questions.prompt: Which apparatus is most suitable for measuring a fixed volume of water?
questions.correctAnswer: Measuring cylinder
questions.explanation: A measuring cylinder has volume markings that help measure liquids accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify apparatus used for measuring volume.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is used to measure force?
questions.correctAnswer: Spring balance
questions.explanation: A spring balance measures force, usually in newtons.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify instruments used to measure force.

questions.prompt: Why should a beaker not be used when a learner needs a very accurate volume reading?
options: Its markings are less precise than a measuring cylinder
It is always made of paper
questions.correctAnswer: Its markings are less precise than a measuring cylinder
questions.explanation: Beakers are useful for holding and mixing liquids, but measuring cylinders give more accurate volume readings.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate apparatus for accurate measurement.

questions.prompt: Which apparatus should be used to hold a hot evaporating dish safely?
questions.correctAnswer: Tongs
questions.explanation: Tongs help hold hot apparatus without touching it directly.
questions.learningOutcome: Handle hot apparatus safely during laboratory work.

questions.prompt: A filter funnel can be used with filter paper when separating an insoluble solid from a liquid.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The funnel supports filter paper, which traps insoluble particles while liquid passes through.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify apparatus used in filtration.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to view tiny details on a leaf surface. Which tool is most suitable?
questions.correctAnswer: Hand lens
questions.explanation: A hand lens magnifies small objects so details can be seen more clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple instruments to observe small objects.

questions.prompt: Which pair is correctly matched?
questions.correctAnswer: Ammeter - measuring electric current
questions.explanation: An ammeter is connected in a circuit to measure electric current.
questions.learningOutcome: Match laboratory instruments with their uses.

questions.prompt: Which care practice helps protect a thermometer after use?
options: Clean it carefully and store it in its case
Use it to stir hot sand
Drop it into a crowded drawer
Hold it by the bulb while shaking it
questions.correctAnswer: Clean it carefully and store it in its case
questions.explanation: A thermometer is fragile and should be cleaned and stored safely to prevent breakage.
questions.learningOutcome: Care for laboratory instruments after use.

questions.prompt: Which example is a mixture?
questions.correctAnswer: Soil
questions.explanation: Soil contains different substances such as mineral particles, humus, air, water, and living organisms.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify mixtures in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a mixture?
options: Two or more substances physically combined
One substance made of only one kind of atom
A substance that cannot be separated by physical methods
A chemical symbol written for an element
questions.correctAnswer: Two or more substances physically combined
questions.explanation: In a mixture, substances are combined physically and can often be separated by physical methods.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of a mixture.

questions.prompt: Which mixture can be separated best by filtration?
questions.correctAnswer: Sand and water
questions.explanation: Sand is insoluble in water, so filter paper can trap it while water passes through.
questions.learningOutcome: Select a suitable method for separating mixtures.

questions.prompt: Which method is most suitable for obtaining salt from salty water?
questions.correctAnswer: Evaporation
questions.explanation: Evaporation removes water as vapour and leaves dissolved salt behind.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply evaporation to separate a dissolved solid from water.

questions.prompt: Which mixture would be separated using a magnet?
questions.correctAnswer: Iron filings and sand
questions.explanation: Iron is magnetic, so a magnet can attract iron filings away from non-magnetic sand.
questions.learningOutcome: Use magnetic separation for suitable mixtures.

questions.prompt: A mixture of maize flour and dry beans can be separated by which simple method?
questions.correctAnswer: Sieving
questions.explanation: Sieving separates solid particles of different sizes using a mesh.
questions.learningOutcome: Use particle size to choose a separation method.

questions.prompt: In decanting, a clear liquid can be carefully poured off from settled solid particles.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Decanting works when heavier insoluble particles settle and the liquid above them is poured away carefully.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe decanting as a method of separating mixtures.

questions.prompt: A learner separates muddy water by letting mud settle, pouring off clearer water, and then filtering. What is the best reason for using two methods?
options: The methods remove different amounts and sizes of solid particles
The second method changes water into an element
questions.correctAnswer: The methods remove different amounts and sizes of solid particles
questions.explanation: Settling removes heavier particles first, while filtration removes smaller insoluble particles that remain suspended.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze why more than one method may be used to separate a mixture.

questions.prompt: Which mixture is homogeneous?
questions.correctAnswer: Salt solution
questions.explanation: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform appearance and composition throughout.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify mixtures as homogeneous or heterogeneous.

questions.prompt: A learner must separate a mixture containing sand, iron filings, and salt. Which sequence is most logical?
options: Use a magnet, add water and filter, then evaporate
Evaporate first, then use a magnet, then add water
Filter first without water, then sieve the salt
Add oil, freeze the mixture, then decant
questions.correctAnswer: Use a magnet, add water and filter, then evaporate
questions.explanation: The magnet removes iron, water dissolves salt, filtration removes sand, and evaporation recovers salt.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a sequence of physical methods to separate a mixture.

questions.prompt: Why is air considered a mixture rather than a single pure substance?
options: It contains several gases such as nitrogen, oxygen, and carbon dioxide
It is always visible in the classroom
It has no mass at all
It cannot move from place to place
questions.correctAnswer: It contains several gases such as nitrogen, oxygen, and carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Air is a physical combination of gases whose proportions can vary slightly from place to place.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why common substances can be classified as mixtures.

questions.prompt: Which household substance is acidic?
questions.correctAnswer: Lemon juice
questions.explanation: Lemon juice contains citric acid, which makes it acidic.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common acidic household substances.

questions.prompt: Which household substance is most likely basic?
questions.correctAnswer: Soap solution
questions.explanation: Many soap solutions are basic and feel slippery because of their alkaline nature.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common basic household substances.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of an indicator in acid-base tests?
options: To show whether a solution is acidic, basic, or neutral
To measure the mass of the solution
To make all solutions safe to drink
questions.correctAnswer: To show whether a solution is acidic, basic, or neutral
questions.explanation: Indicators change colour depending on the acidity or basicity of a solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the use of indicators in testing solutions.

questions.prompt: Which plant material can be used to prepare a simple natural indicator?
questions.correctAnswer: Red cabbage leaves
questions.explanation: Some coloured plant extracts change colour in acids and bases, so they can act as indicators.
questions.learningOutcome: Use plant extracts as acid-base indicators.

questions.prompt: A universal indicator can help estimate how strong an acid or base is.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Universal indicator gives a range of colours that can be compared with a pH scale.
questions.learningOutcome: Use universal indicator to compare acidity and basicity.

questions.prompt: A solution has pH 3. What does this show?
questions.correctAnswer: It is acidic
questions.explanation: Solutions with pH values below 7 are acidic.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret simple pH values for acids and bases.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares acids and bases?
options: Acids have pH below 7 while bases have pH above 7
Acids and bases always have pH 7
All acids are safe to taste in the laboratory
questions.correctAnswer: Acids have pH below 7 while bases have pH above 7
questions.explanation: The pH scale classifies acidic, neutral, and basic solutions by their pH values.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare acidic, neutral, and basic solutions.

questions.prompt: A farmer adds lime to acidic soil. What is the purpose of this practice?
options: To remove all nutrients from soil
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce soil acidity
questions.explanation: Lime is basic and can help neutralize excess acidity in soil.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate acids and bases to real-life applications.

questions.prompt: A learner tests three drinks with a plant indicator. Which record would be most useful for comparison?
options: A table showing each drink and the colour change
A drawing of the learner's favourite bottle
A list of drink prices only
A paragraph saying all drinks look nice
questions.correctAnswer: A table showing each drink and the colour change
questions.explanation: A table links each sample to its result, making comparison and classification easier.
questions.learningOutcome: Record and compare results from acid-base indicator tests.

questions.prompt: Which source of water is most likely to contain mud and other solid impurities after heavy rain?
options: Water sealed in a laboratory reagent bottle
questions.correctAnswer: River water
questions.explanation: Runoff after heavy rain can carry soil, plant remains, and other solids into rivers.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify nearby sources of water that may contain impurities.

questions.prompt: Which material in a simple water filter mainly traps larger solid particles?
questions.correctAnswer: Gravel
questions.explanation: Gravel has spaces that allow water through while holding back larger particles.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify materials used in a simple water filter.

questions.prompt: Why is charcoal sometimes used in a homemade water filter?
options: It can absorb some colour and smell from water
It changes dirty water into pure oxygen
It makes all germs disappear instantly
It dissolves sand into the water
questions.correctAnswer: It can absorb some colour and smell from water
questions.explanation: Charcoal can remove some dissolved impurities, colour, and smell, but filtered water may still need further treatment before drinking.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of filter materials in water purification.

questions.prompt: Clear filtered water is always safe to drink without any further treatment.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Filtered water may still contain disease-causing microorganisms, so safe treatment such as boiling may be needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why filtered water may need further treatment before drinking.

questions.prompt: Which arrangement is most suitable for a simple bottle water filter from top to bottom?
options: Plastic paper, metal nails, salt, ash
Only large stones with no lower layer
questions.correctAnswer: Gravel, sand, charcoal, cotton cloth
questions.explanation: Layered materials can remove particles of different sizes and some impurities as water passes through.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a simple water filter using locally available materials.

questions.prompt: Which community action would best help keep river water cleaner over a long period?
options: Prevent dumping of waste into the river
Wash pesticide containers directly in the river
Cut all vegetation along river banks
Let livestock stand in the water daily
questions.correctAnswer: Prevent dumping of waste into the river
questions.explanation: Reducing waste at the source is a long-term way to protect water quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore sustainable strategies for keeping community water sources clean.

questions.prompt: A group wants to compare two homemade filters fairly. Which plan is best?
options: Use equal amounts of the same muddy water and compare clarity after filtering
Use clean water in one filter and muddy water in the other
Change the water amount, filter size, and materials at once
Judge the filters by the colour of their bottles
questions.correctAnswer: Use equal amounts of the same muddy water and compare clarity after filtering
questions.explanation: A fair comparison keeps most conditions the same and changes only the filter design or material being tested.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan a fair test to compare water purification methods.

questions.prompt: What is menstruation?
options: The monthly shedding of the uterine lining when pregnancy has not occurred
The movement of air into the lungs
The removal of sweat from the skin only
The growth of nails and hair
questions.correctAnswer: The monthly shedding of the uterine lining when pregnancy has not occurred
questions.explanation: Menstruation is part of the menstrual cycle and involves bleeding as the uterine lining leaves the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the menstrual cycle in human beings.

questions.prompt: Which event takes place during fertilization in humans?
options: A sperm cell fuses with an egg cell
questions.correctAnswer: A sperm cell fuses with an egg cell
questions.explanation: Fertilization occurs when the male gamete and female gamete join to form a zygote.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the process of fertilization in human beings.

questions.prompt: Where does implantation normally occur after fertilization?
options: In the wall of the uterus
questions.correctAnswer: In the wall of the uterus
questions.explanation: Implantation is the attachment of the early embryo to the lining of the uterus.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe implantation in human beings.

questions.prompt: Menstrual hygiene includes using clean materials, changing them regularly, and disposing of them safely.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Good menstrual hygiene helps prevent discomfort, infection, odour, and stigma.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe healthy practices for managing menstruation.

questions.prompt: Which challenge may be related to the menstrual cycle for some learners?
questions.correctAnswer: Abdominal cramps
questions.explanation: Some people experience cramps, discomfort, mood changes, or irregular cycles during menstruation.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe challenges related to the menstrual cycle.

questions.prompt: Which response is most supportive when a classmate has menstrual discomfort at school?
options: Encourage them to seek help from a trusted adult or health worker
Mock them in front of classmates
Force them to continue a painful activity
questions.correctAnswer: Encourage them to seek help from a trusted adult or health worker
questions.explanation: Respectful support protects dignity and helps the learner get appropriate care.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate respectful management of challenges related to menstruation.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best shows early human reproduction after release of an egg?
questions.correctAnswer: Fertilization, zygote formation, implantation
questions.explanation: After fertilization, the zygote divides and the developing embryo implants in the uterus lining.
questions.learningOutcome: Sequence fertilization and implantation events in human reproduction.

questions.prompt: Why should menstruation be discussed respectfully in school science lessons?
options: It is a normal body process and learners need accurate health information
It is unrelated to health or human biology
It should only be used for teasing
It prevents learners from studying other topics
questions.correctAnswer: It is a normal body process and learners need accurate health information
questions.explanation: Respectful discussion reduces stigma and supports health, dignity, and informed decision-making.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of accurate and respectful reproductive health learning.

questions.prompt: A learner is planning a school awareness poster on menstrual hygiene. Which message is most accurate?
options: Use clean absorbent materials and dispose of used materials safely
Keep used materials anywhere in the classroom
Avoid washing hands after changing materials
Share personal items without cleaning them
questions.correctAnswer: Use clean absorbent materials and dispose of used materials safely
questions.explanation: Clean materials, handwashing, and safe disposal are important parts of menstrual hygiene.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an accurate health message about menstrual hygiene.

questions.prompt: Which waste product is removed from the body through sweat?
questions.correctAnswer: Excess water and salts
questions.explanation: Sweat contains water, salts, and small amounts of other wastes released through sweat glands.
questions.subStrandTitle: Human Excretory System: Skin and Kidneys
questions.learningOutcome: Identify waste products excreted through the skin.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of the kidneys?
questions.correctAnswer: Filter blood and form urine
questions.explanation: Kidneys remove wastes and excess substances from blood to form urine.
questions.subStrandTitle: Human Excretory System: Skin and Kidneys
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the function of the kidneys in excretion.

questions.prompt: Which external part of the skin allows sweat to leave the body?
questions.correctAnswer: Sweat pore
questions.explanation: Sweat pores are small openings on the skin surface through which sweat is released.
questions.subStrandTitle: Human Excretory System: Skin and Kidneys
questions.learningOutcome: Identify external parts of the human skin and their functions.

questions.prompt: Drinking enough clean water can help support kidney function.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Adequate clean water helps the kidneys remove wastes from the blood through urine.
questions.subStrandTitle: Human Excretory System: Skin and Kidneys
questions.learningOutcome: Adopt healthy practices that promote kidney health.

questions.prompt: Which habit can help keep the skin healthy?
options: Bathing regularly with clean water and mild soap
questions.correctAnswer: Bathing regularly with clean water and mild soap
questions.explanation: Regular washing removes sweat, dirt, and microorganisms that can affect skin health.
questions.subStrandTitle: Human Excretory System: Skin and Kidneys
questions.learningOutcome: Adopt healthy practices that promote skin health.

questions.prompt: Which choice is a possible cause of kidney disorders?
questions.correctAnswer: Untreated urinary infections
questions.explanation: Some untreated infections can spread or damage parts of the urinary system, including the kidneys.
questions.subStrandTitle: Human Excretory System: Skin and Kidneys
questions.learningOutcome: Describe causes of kidney disorders.

questions.prompt: Why can misuse of some cosmetics harm the skin?
options: Some may contain harsh chemicals that irritate or damage skin
All cosmetics make kidneys filter faster
Cosmetics remove the need for hygiene
questions.correctAnswer: Some may contain harsh chemicals that irritate or damage skin
questions.explanation: Unsafe or misused skin products can cause irritation, burns, infections, or long-term damage.
questions.subStrandTitle: Human Excretory System: Skin and Kidneys
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of proper use of cosmetics for skin health.

questions.prompt: A learner has a deep skin cut after falling. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Seek first aid and keep the wound clean
Rub soil on it to stop bleeding
Share unclean cloth with many people
questions.correctAnswer: Seek first aid and keep the wound clean
questions.explanation: Proper first aid reduces bleeding, pain, and the risk of infection.
questions.subStrandTitle: Human Excretory System: Skin and Kidneys
questions.learningOutcome: Apply healthy practices for protecting the skin.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why excretion is important?
options: It removes wastes that could harm body cells if they build up
It separates sand from water only
It makes all foods taste sweet
questions.correctAnswer: It removes wastes that could harm body cells if they build up
questions.explanation: Excretion helps maintain a healthier internal environment by removing metabolic wastes and excess substances.
questions.subStrandTitle: Human Excretory System: Skin and Kidneys
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of excretion in the human body.

questions.prompt: Which activity can produce static electricity?
options: Rubbing a balloon on dry hair
questions.correctAnswer: Rubbing a balloon on dry hair
questions.explanation: Rubbing can transfer electric charges between materials, causing static electricity.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate the existence of static charges in objects.

questions.prompt: Why can a rubbed plastic ruler attract small pieces of paper?
options: The ruler has gained static charge
The paper has changed into metal
The ruler has become hotter than fire
The paper has dissolved in air
questions.correctAnswer: The ruler has gained static charge
questions.explanation: A charged object can attract light neutral objects because charges inside them shift slightly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain effects of forces between charged objects.

questions.prompt: Like electric charges repel each other while unlike charges attract each other.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Objects with the same type of charge push apart, while objects with opposite charges pull together.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe attraction and repulsion between charged objects.

questions.prompt: Which safety measure is best during a thunderstorm with lightning?
options: Stay indoors away from tall isolated trees
Hold a metal rod in an open field
Swim in a river until rain stops
questions.correctAnswer: Stay indoors away from tall isolated trees
questions.explanation: Lightning is a dangerous electrical discharge, so shelter indoors is safer than open spaces or tall isolated trees.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safety measures when dealing with static charges and lightning.

questions.prompt: A charged comb attracts paper bits but later stops attracting them strongly. What is the best explanation?
options: The comb lost some charge to the surroundings
The comb turned into a magnet
Gravity stopped acting on the paper
questions.correctAnswer: The comb lost some charge to the surroundings
questions.explanation: Static charge can leak away through moist air, handling, or contact with other materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze changes in the effect of static charges over time.

questions.prompt: Which method charges an object without direct contact with the charged object?
questions.correctAnswer: Induction
questions.explanation: Charging by induction uses a nearby charged object to rearrange charges without touching it directly.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify different methods of charging objects.

questions.prompt: How could a learner design a safe demonstration of static electricity in class?
options: Rub a plastic ruler with dry cloth and test attraction on tiny paper pieces
Connect bare wires directly to a wall socket
Stand outside in lightning to observe charges
Mix unknown chemicals in a beaker
questions.correctAnswer: Rub a plastic ruler with dry cloth and test attraction on tiny paper pieces
questions.explanation: A rubbed ruler and small paper pieces provide a simple, low-risk way to observe static attraction.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a safe demonstration showing the existence of static charges.

questions.prompt: Which is a renewable source of electricity used in Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Geothermal steam
questions.explanation: Kenya uses geothermal energy from underground heat to generate electricity.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sources of electricity in the environment.

questions.prompt: In a simple circuit, what is the function of a switch?
options: To open or close the circuit
To store all water in the circuit
questions.correctAnswer: To open or close the circuit
questions.explanation: A switch controls whether electric current can flow through a circuit.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe parts and functions in simple electrical circuits.

questions.prompt: Which material is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.correctAnswer: Copper wire
questions.explanation: Copper allows electric current to pass through it easily and is commonly used in electrical wiring.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify materials as conductors and non-conductors of electricity.

Use damaged cables until they spark
Overload one socket with many appliances

questions.prompt: A bulb in a simple circuit does not light. Which first check is most reasonable?

Replace copper wires with dry sticks

questions.prompt: A learner must sort mixed classroom materials into magnetic and non-magnetic groups. Which plan is best?

Guess from the colour of each item only

questions.correctAnswer: Test each item with a magnet and record whether it is attracted
